To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphology and elasticity of living cultured macrophages (cells) can be investigated with an atomic force microscopy (AFM) in physiological buffer for several hours without damage to the cells.
the morphology and elasticity of living cultured rat macrophages can be investigated by AFM.
the AFM can be used as a tool to investigate living cells in their physiological environment and that the elastic modulus of living macrophages is mainly determined by the actin‐based cytoskeleton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to investigate the mechanical properties of living cells with the AFM.
the application of an AFM to study the mechanical properties of living cells in a quantitative manner.
the development of AFM as a new tool to study living cells and the cytoskeleton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the actin‐cytoskeleton is the major contributor to the elastic modulus in living macrophages, and that the elastic modulus of the actin‐free cytoplasm is significantly lower than that of the intact cell.
the elastic properties of the living cells are determined by the underlying cytoskeleton.
the elastic properties of the cells are determined by the actin cytoskeleton and are strongly dependent on the cell's shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytoskeleton is responsible for the cell's elasticity and that the AFM is an appropriate tool to study living cells in their natural environment.
living cells can be investigated with AFM and that the mechanical properties of cells can be measured with nanometer spatial resolution.
AFM is a powerful technique for studying the mechanical properties of living cells and their cytoskeleton.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoskeleton plays a crucial role in the mechanical properties of cells, and AFM is a powerful tool to measure the elastic properties of cells and their sub‐structures in real‐time.
the AFM is a powerful tool for studying living cells and their dynamics in physiological conditions.
AFM can be used for the investigation of living cultured cells in a noninvasive way.
